The image shows a corn ear with husks pulled back. Key observations:
- Ear with visible kernel rot
- Pinkish-red to brownish discoloration covering the kernels
- White-pink mold/mycelium visible on kernel surfaces
- The rot appears to start from the tip or distributed across the ear
- No green or olive coloration (rules out Trichoderma/Aspergillus)
- Not pure white cottony growth (rules out Diplodia)

The pink-to-red mycelial growth on the kernels is the hallmark of **Gibberella ear rot** (caused by *Fusarium graminearum*), which produces a distinctive pink/red mold that often starts at the tip of the ear and progresses toward the base.
